title.narrative: Policies and programmes developed and implemented to promote and improve safety and health at work

description.narrative: The ILO is supporting Belize in modernizing its occupational safety and health (OSH) framework through a landmark OSH Bill, introduced in the House of Representatives in June 2025. Expected to take effect by year-end, the Bill replaces the outdated Factories Act and aligns with ILO Conventions No. 155 and No. 187, as well as Belize’s Decent Work Country Programme 2024–2029. Developed through extensive consultation and technical assistance, the Bill strengthens OSH governance by establishing a National OSH Advisory Committee and a dedicated OSH Inspectorate within the Ministry of Labour. It also sets the stage for a future standalone OSH Authority. Key provisions include clear responsibilities for all workplace actors, whistleblower protection, mandatory incident reporting, workplace safety committees, and enforcement tools such as improvement notices, prohibition orders, and administrative penalties. By reducing workplace accidents and illnesses, the new law will improve worker well-being, boost productivity, and ease pressure on social protection systems.
